title: SO(3)-Equivariant Learning on CAD Boundary Representations
claim: Heterogeneous inputs are encoded through parallel feature paths, then fused into equivariant node features for a graph network.
layout: Left-to-right, three stacked parallel encoder panels merging into a fusion box, then a graph
description: A left-to-right pipeline diagram. At far left, a gray 3D CAD bracket is exploded into separate B-rep faces. The faces feed a central boxed column with three stacked paths. The first is Surface attributes: surface-type icons, an area label m², and a local frame with u, v and n axes. The second is Surface geometry & trimming: a UV grid of points feeding a CNN drawn as gray blocks. The third is Ray field: a bracket with blue outgoing and orange incoming rays, and spherical-harmonic blobs labeled OUT and IN. Each path outputs scalar, vector or matrix feature icons, drawn as blue squares, thin bars and grids. These merge into a rounded Feature fusion box. The result is h_i^(0), h_i^(1), h_i^(2), which feed a black-and-gray Face-adjacency graph. A legend at bottom right defines the icons for ℓ=0, 1 and 2.
caption: Face feature construction. Each B-rep face is initialized with features from three encoding paths before message passing. Surface attributes ($\ell{=}0,1$): surface-type and log-area scalars, plus the three LRF axes as $\ell{=}1$ channels. Surface geometry and trimming ($\ell{=}0$): a CNN on the UV grid, expressed in the LRF. Ray field ($\ell{=}0,1,2$): a spherical-harmonic (SH) encoding of rays cast over two hemispheres, with ray directions fixed in the LRF. Feature fusion combines the scalars and projects all paths equivariantly to the GNN input features $h_i^{(\ell)}$, with $C_\ell$ channels for each degree $\ell \in \{0,1,2\}$.
abstract: Learning on boundary representations (B-reps) requires robustness to the pose of a part, since CAD models are not stored in a canonical orientation. Existing B-rep networks either operate on world-frame coordinates and normals, and thus degrade under rotation, or encode each face in a local reference frame. Local frames yield invariance, but reduce inter-face messages to scalars and discard the relative orientation of adjacent faces. We propose SO3brep, an SO(3)-equivariant graph neural network on the B-rep face-adjacency graph. Node features are computed in local frames and mapped into a shared frame by Wigner D-matrices. Clebsch-Gordan tensor products couple these features with the directions between adjacent faces, so that relative orientation is preserved throughout message passing and the output remains SE(3)-invariant. Across three face-segmentation and two classification benchmarks with randomly rotated test parts, SO3brep achieves the highest accuracy among the compared B-rep networks and equivariant point cloud networks, with the fewest parameters. Its advantage is largest with few labeled parts, a setting typical of industrial CAD. Code is available at https://github.com/UGent-CVAMO/so3brep.
